title: Ned in the Frost
checkpoint: Reception Summer 1, week 2 — Phase 4: CCVC words: two consonant sounds together at the start (no new sounds)
note_for_grown_ups: No new letters here — this is Phase 4, where children blend longer words with two consonants side by side (fr-ost, cr-isp, st-and). Encourage sounding each consonant on its own: 'f-r-o-s-t', not 'fr'.

pages.text: Pip and Ned went for a trek.
pages.illustration: Pip and Ned setting off across a frosted field at first light, small against a wide pale winter sky. Their breath shows. Long blue shadows on white grass.
The pair leaning hard into a strong wind, feathers and down blown flat backwards, bare branches bending behind them. Cold blues and greys.

pages.text: Frost sat on all the grass.
pages.illustration: Extreme close-up of frost crystals along a single blade of grass, drawn like tiny white ferns. No characters. Beautiful and quiet.

pages.text: They stand on the crisp, stiff grass.
pages.illustration: Two sets of feet on stiff white grass, seen from ground level, with the grass visibly crunching flat under them. Playful low viewpoint.

pages.text: A twig did snap and crack.
pages.illustration: A twig snapping underfoot, shown as the break itself with two split ends and a spray of frost. Ned mid-air with fright.

pages.text: Ned had to jump the pond.
pages.illustration: Ned crouched at the near bank of the frozen-edged pond, tail up, about to launch across. Full of coiled energy. The far bank looks a long way.

pages.text: Splash! Ned fell in with a plop.
pages.illustration: Ned belly-flopped into the cold water with an enormous flat splash, only his tail and one foot above the surface. Pip's beak open in horror.

pages.text: Pip must help Ned up the ramp.
pages.illustration: Pip hauling on Ned's flipper from the bank with both feet braced, absolutely straining. Ned half out, plastered with mud and weed. Very funny.

pages.text: Ned was damp, but he was glad.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the two of them side by side on the frosty bank, Ned soaked and steaming faintly, both grinning. Low winter sun breaking through.
